Could you tell me whether the Moon would be visible to me at the moment?

I'm in Alice Springs, Australia at 2026-11-10 18:27 ACST (UTC+0930) (2026-11-10T08:57:00Z in UTC), at latitude -23.698 degrees and longitude 133.8807 degrees. My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is 5.086 degrees and its azimuth is 253.378 degrees, so it is above the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is 16.793 degrees and its azimuth is 249.764 degrees, so it is above the horizon. The Moon is 1.32 percent illuminated, 13.169 degrees from the Sun, and 398861.4 kilometers away. The sky brightness is bright daylight, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Probably not with unaided eyesight.

The Moon is technically above the horizon at altitude **16.8°**, but it is an extremely thin crescent—only **1.32% illuminated**—and lies just **13.2° from the Sun**. With the Sun still **5.1° above the horizon**, the sky will remain bright, and the illuminated lunar sliver will be very faint against the daylight. Atmospheric haze near the horizon makes this even harder.

An experienced observer using binoculars or a telescope might locate it, especially with the precise position and a very clear, transparent sky. But for an ordinary unaided observer, even knowing where to look, it would be **very unlikely to spot**, and attempting to sweep the area with binoculars would be unsafe while the Sun is above the horizon. Once the Sun has set, the Moon will also be setting soon and may be below the horizon before the sky becomes dark enough.
